description:
REVIEWED 2026-10-25 (TodoReview) against origin/develop 9a184b619 and fork main ea44bcc9 (30.24.0.13). PROBLEM
Since v0.4.1 translated SQL for some platforms carries explicit NULLS LAST modifiers (found by the published-results audit: TSBS DevOps and DataVault Q11). No reviewed PR's published-impact section names it. Whether the placement matches the benchmark's intent, and whether published results changed, is undetermined.

VERIFIED FACTS (2026-10-25, executed with the vendored fork 30.24.0.13 on an origin/develop export)
- The original description was imprecise. It is not DESC-only and not Snowflake/Databricks-only:
  * DataVault Q11: Snowflake `ORDER BY value DESC NULLS LAST`; Databricks `ORDER BY `value` DESC` (plain, no modifier); BigQuery plain; DuckDB plain.
  * TSBS DevOps (18 queries): Snowflake emits `DESC NULLS LAST` on 10; Databricks and BigQuery each emit `ORDER BY `time` NULLS LAST` (ASCENDING with an explicit NULLS LAST) on 6. On Spark/Databricks and BigQuery the ASC default is NULLS FIRST, so these are non-default placements; on Snowflake the DESC default is NULLS FIRST (NULLs are large), so `DESC NULLS LAST` is non-default too.
- Mechanism: stock SQLGlot NULL_ORDERING logic (`nulls_are_small` default, Snowflake `nulls_are_large` in sqlglot/dialects/snowflake.py), not a fork patch. The output depends on the SOURCE dialect of each benchmark's text: fork probe `ORDER BY a DESC` duckdb->snowflake `DESC NULLS LAST`, duckdb->databricks plain; netezza->snowflake plain but netezza->duckdb `DESC NULLS FIRST`; postgres->databricks `DESC NULLS FIRST`. So the explicit modifiers preserve a DuckDB/ClickHouse-style 'NULLs last' source semantics on engines whose defaults differ.
- The earlier claim that the modifier is a no-op on Databricks does not hold for the queries checked: it is plain DESC there but explicit NULLS LAST on ASC keys.
- Published bundles for TSBS and DataVault exist (cloud and local); bundles store row counts and timings, not result rows, so order/LIMIT-membership changes cannot be read back from them.

DECISION GATES (stop and ask the owner)
G1 Intended NULL placement per benchmark (decide with the benchmark specification text in hand: check TPC-H/TPC-DS/TSBS/DataVault wording on NULL ordering before choosing). Options: (a) keep explicit source-semantics placement on every engine (current behaviour; cross-engine comparable and equal to the DuckDB reference; recommended default); (b) engine-native defaults (drop the modifiers; engines then disagree on NULL keys); (c) one explicit placement (e.g. NULLS FIRST for ASC, LAST for DESC) for all engines. 
G2 Published impact. If a nullable sort key feeds a LIMIT or an order-sensitive validation, decide how to mark the affected bundles: sidecar flag with a new closed-vocabulary defect id, or CORPUS_NOTES note only. New id = results-policy change = owner approval.
G3 Any change to emitted text is a translation change: needs the fork PR + wheel-bump flow and, for cloud-only engines, owner approval before any cloud verification.

GUARDRAILS
- Do not change sort semantics to 'fix' a perceived difference before G1 is decided.
- No cloud spend; Snowflake and BigQuery have no engine in fork CI: evidence is a documented gap plus vendor documentation of default NULL ordering (link it), Spark (pyspark) in fork CI stands in for Databricks and DuckDB for the reference.
- Published bundles are never edited.

TRANSLATION-CHANGE CHECKS (any BenchBox PR that changes emitted SQL): `make sql-execution-gate`, `make compat-docs-check`, `make typecheck`, `make comment-policy-check`, `BENCHBOX_QUESTDB_DSN=postgresql://admin:quest@127.0.0.1:8812/qdb make sqlglot-repro-retirement-check`. SQL translation fixes land in the fork BenchBox-dev/benchbox-sqlglot (clone /Users/joe/Developer/sqlglot) with a real-engine test in fork CI or a documented gap in downstream/ENGINE-GAPS.md; BenchBox adopts via a wheel-bump PR carrying `make sqlglot-fork-diff` output.
STANDING GUARDRAILS: work only in a `make worktree-create` worktree after `make agent-write-preflight` (primary clone /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox is read-only); run tests only through make targets (`make test-fast`, `make pr-preflight`, `make sql-execution-gate`, `make tpcds-obt-equivalence`) or targeted `uv run -- python -m pytest <paths> -n 4`; never BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR, `make test-unlock` or raw broad runs; one heavy run at a time; no live-cloud spend and no production publish without explicit owner approval; published result bundles are never edited (only manifest-sidecar `known_defects` and results-data/CORPUS_NOTES.md per results-data/DEFECTIVE_DATAGEN_AUDIT.md); no SKIP / --no-verify / `git add -A`; no explanatory comments or docstrings in code (`make comment-policy-check`); uv only; identity Joe Harris, no Co-Authored-By; PR flow `make pr-preflight` once, `make pr-open`, CI + oracle review, `make pr-arm`. Stop and ask the owner on unexpected result changes, relaxed guards, oracle stand-ins or real design choices.
